title: Add burst pool dashboards + alert rules (saturation, rejects, neighbor p99 drift)
author: Sergio Costa
release_notes: Internal-only: Adds Grafana dashboards and alerting rules for Dedicated burst pools (saturation, reject rate, and neighbor p99 drift).
body:
Summary: This PR adds the initial burst-capacity observability surface to the observability-pack repo: (1) Grafana dashboards for burst pool health and per-tenant visibility (with cardinality-safe defaults), and (2) alerts-as-code rules covering burst pool saturation, admission reject spikes, and potential noisy-neighbor risk via dedicated baseline p99 drift correlated with burst saturation. This is intended to support the ENG-4827 pilot readiness checklist and aligns with the burst admission SLOs/guardrails work in the redwood monorepo.

Context / Why: During pilot load tests we could see burst pools saturate, but we didn’t have a consistent dashboard/alert bundle to answer: which pool/region is hot, what is being rejected (and why), and are baseline Dedicated tenants seeing tail latency drift correlated with burst activity. SRE requested explicit paging policy and thresholds for burst reject rates and neighbor p99 drift, with clear runbook links.

What’s included: Dashboard: Dedicated > Burst Pools Overview (folder: Dedicated/Burst). Panels: (a) Burst pool saturation (gpu_utilization + queue depth proxy) by region/pool, (b) Admission outcomes (admit/deny) with deny reason breakdown, (c) Burst request TPS + tokens/sec (aggregate), (d) Baseline Dedicated p99 latency vs historical baseline overlay, (e) Correlation panel: burst saturation vs baseline p99 drift. Dashboard: Dedicated > Burst Tenant Drilldown. Panels: (a) Burst usage (requests/tokens) by tenant_id (templated variable; hidden by default + sampling note), (b) Reject rate by tenant_id, (c) Top models by burst tokens, (d) Burst cooldown/circuit-breaker activations (if metric present). Note: tenant-level panels are explicitly marked “for incident/debug; do not alert” and default to off in shared links.

Alerts (Prometheus rule groups): Group: dedicated-burst-pools. Alerts: (1) BurstPoolSaturationHigh: triggers when pool_saturation_ratio > 0.90 for 10m OR (gpu_utilization > 0.92 AND burst_queue_depth > threshold) for 10m; labels include region, pool, gpu_type. Severity: page (pilot) / ticket (post-GA TBD). Runbook: runbook-burst-pool-saturation. (2) BurstAdmissionRejectRateHigh: triggers when reject_rate > 0.15 for 5m AND admit_requests_rate > minimum to avoid low-traffic noise; excludes deny_reason=cooldown only (cooldown-only bursts are expected under sustained spike; still visible in dashboards). Severity: ticket by default; page if combined with saturation. (3) DedicatedNeighborP99DriftCorrelated: triggers when (baseline_dedicated_p99_ms increases by >20% vs 1h baseline) AND burst_pool_saturation_ratio > 0.85 in same region for 10m. This is intentionally correlation-gated to avoid paging on unrelated latency events. Severity: page during pilot.

Metric assumptions / naming: This PR assumes telemetry work in ENG-4826 emitting (names representative): redwood_burst_admission_total{result="admit|deny", reason="...", region="...", pool="..."}, redwood_burst_pool_saturation_ratio{region,pool,gpu_type}, redwood_dedicated_request_latency_ms_bucket{tier="baseline", region="..."} (or equivalent). Where metric names differ across environments, the dashboards use a small set of recording rules already present in this repo; see “Implementation notes” below.

Implementation notes: - Added recording rules to normalize burst admission rates and reject rate calculations, to keep dashboard queries fast and consistent. - Alerts avoid tenant_id and model in label sets to prevent cardinality blowups; tenant/model drilldowns remain in dashboards only (templated variable is opt-in). - All new alerts include runbook_url annotations and a short “what to check first” section pointing to the Burst Pools Overview dashboard.

Changed files / areas: - dashboards/dedicated/burst/burst_pools_overview.jsonnet (new) - dashboards/dedicated/burst/burst_tenant_drilldown.jsonnet (new) - alerts/dedicated/burst_pools.rules.yaml (new) - rules/dedicated/burst_recording.rules.yaml (new) - dashboards/README.md (add folder + ownership note) - provisioning/folders/dedicated.yaml (add Burst folder)

Small illustrative snippets: - Alert correlation gate:
expr: (dedicated_baseline_p99_ms{region=~"$region"} > (1.2 * dedicated_baseline_p99_ms:avg_over_time_1h{region=~"$region"})) and on(region) (burst_pool_saturation_ratio{region=~"$region"} > 0.85)
for: 10m
annotations:
  summary: "Dedicated baseline p99 drift correlated with burst saturation ({{ $labels.region }})"
  runbook_url: "https://confluence.redwoodinference.com/display/SRE/runbook-burst-pool-saturation"

Testing / CI: - grafonnet-lint: pass - dashboard-compile (jsonnet -> json): pass - promtool rules test: pass - snapshots: regenerated for new dashboards

Rollout / Ops notes: - These assets are safe to deploy ahead of GA; alerts are scoped to the pilot clusters via existing environment selectors. - Paging policy defaults to pilot-only (see labels: pilot_only="true"); SRE can flip to broader on-call after ENG-4827 signoff. - If reject-rate alert is noisy, recommended first tweak is increase minimum traffic gate and extend for: window.

Links: - Linear: ENG-4827 (Dashboards + alert rules for burst saturation and neighbor SLO risk) - Runbook: Confluence runbook-burst-pool-saturation - Related telemetry: ENG-4826 (metrics emission + cardinality controls)

Review notes / follow-ups: - TODO(ENG-49xx): once deny reason codes stabilize, add a small panel legend mapping reason -> meaning to reduce confusion during incident response. - TODO: confirm final p99 drift threshold with SRE after the next game day (current is 20%/10m gated by saturation).

Conversation: Allison Grant (review): Can we avoid tenant_id in any alert labels? We’ve been burned by cardinality before. Sergio Costa (author): Yep — alerts are region/pool/gpu_type only. Tenant_id is only used in the drilldown dashboard and is opt-in via variable; also added a note in the dashboard header that tenant drilldowns are incident-only. Logan Wright (review): Metric names in here match the draft; please use recording rules to shield us if the final names change slightly. Sergio Costa (author): Done in this revision: added rules/dedicated/burst_recording.rules.yaml and updated all dashboards/alerts to use the recorded series (dedicated_burst_*). Aisha Bello (review): Reject-rate alert: I’m worried cooldown-only denials will fire constantly during expected sustained spikes. Maybe exclude deny_reason=cooldown? Sergio Costa (author): Updated: reject-rate alert excludes deny_reason=cooldown (still visible in dashboard). Also added traffic floor gate to reduce low-volume noise. Sean Gallagher (review): For neighbor p99 drift, can we gate it on saturation to avoid paging on generic latency events? Sergio Costa (author): Added correlation gate: baseline p99 drift AND burst saturation > 0.85 in same region for 10m. Also added direct link to Burst Pools Overview dashboard in annotations. Peter Holtz (review): Dashboard looks good. Can we add a panel showing baseline vs burst request mix so it’s obvious whether burst is actually being used? Sergio Costa (author): Added “Burst share of Dedicated traffic (req/s)” panel using dedicated_burst_admit_rate / dedicated_total_rate (aggregate) with a note about interpretation.

Merge: Merged via squash into main after approvals (Allison Grant, Aisha Bello, Logan Wright) and green CI.
